one_liner: Pure-Julia recursive LU (Toledo's algorithm) that beats OpenBLAS and often MKL getrf on dense matrices up to about 500x500.
what_it_does: Computes a dense LU factorization with partial pivoting (or none) and returns a standard LinearAlgebra.LU object, so ldiv!, F.L, F.U and F.p work as with LAPACK getrf. Nothing is exported: call RecursiveFactorization.lu(A), lu!(A) or lu!(A, ipiv, pivot, thread). Since 2026 it also ships a random-butterfly-transform solver (the 🦋workspace/🦋solve! path) that skips pivoting. Most users reach it through LinearSolve.jl's RFLUFactorization, which LinearSolve picks by default for square Float32/Float64 systems of N <= 100, N <= 500 under OpenBLAS, or N <= 200 under MKL (Accelerate wins on Apple).
how_it_is_fast: Sivan Toledo's recursive left-looking LU (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl., DOI 10.1137/S0895479896297744) splits the column panel in two, factors the left half recursively, applies the pivots, does a unit-lower triangular solve (TriangularSolve.jl) and a Schur-complement update, then recurses on the right half; this keeps working sets cache-sized without hand-picked block sizes. The Schur update and the base-case kernels are LoopVectorization @turbo loops that JIT-compile SIMD micro-kernels for the host CPU, so there is no BLAS call and none of the threading or dispatch overhead that dominates OpenBLAS at small N. Threading (Polyester @batch / @tturbo) only switches on when the matrix exceeds about 92% of L2 cache.
when_to_use: Repeated dense LU solves of square Float64/Float32 matrices from roughly 10x10 to 500x500 in Julia (ODE/DAE Jacobians, Newton steps, small FEM blocks).
On x86-64 with OpenBLAS as Julia's default BLAS, where SciMLBenchmarks shows about 2x OpenBLAS around N=100-250 on an EPYC 7502.
Inside LinearSolve.jl: load the package and the default algorithm already routes small square systems to RFLUFactorization.
When you want pure-Julia code that also handles ComplexF32/ComplexF64 and non-BLAS element types through the same API (tested in runtests.jl, via the generic recursion path).
when_not_to_use: Large matrices (well above N=500): the only benchmark stops at 500 and LinearSolve itself hands larger sizes back to BLAS/MKL.
From C or C++: it is a Julia package with no C ABI; use a LAPACK getrf (or ReLAPACK) instead.
On Apple Silicon, where LinearSolve's own default prefers Apple Accelerate LU over RFLU.
When you need other factorizations: only LU is implemented (Cholesky and QR are not; issue #74 asks about QR).
Inside an outer Threads.@threads loop with thread=Val(true): issue #48 reports Julia exiting silently on Windows 10; pass Val(false) for the thread argument.

integration.dependencies: LinearAlgebra, LoopVectorization, Polyester, PrecompileTools, SparseBandedMatrices, StrideArraysCore, TriangularSolve, VectorizedRNG
integration.platforms: any platform LoopVectorization supports; recursion threshold is tuned for AVX2 vs AVX-512 (40 vs 48 columns)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; separate matrices can be factored from different tasks, but nested threading with thread=Val(true) has a crash report on Windows (issue #48)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — returns a LinearAlgebra.LU usable wherever LinearAlgebra.lu! output is, but you call RecursiveFactorization.lu! explicitly (or select RFLUFactorization in LinearSolve); it does not replace the BLAS/LAPACK library

gotchas: Direct calls default to single-threaded (thread = Val(false)) while LinearSolve's RFLUFactorization defaults to thread = Val(true); timings differ accordingly, and threading only engages above about 0.92x the L2 cache size.

Fast path needs a StridedArray of Float32/Float64; other array types or element types fall back to a generic (slower) recursion, and pivoted matrices with min(m,n) < 10 go straight to LinearAlgebra.generic_lufact!.
pivot = Val(false) (and the butterfly path) trades stability for speed; LinearSolve's docs say the butterfly variant is less robust for matrices that need pivoting.

A commit of 2026-08-08 ('Initialize a user-supplied ipiv in pivot-free lu!') fixed no-pivot mode returning a user-supplied ipiv full of uninitialized memory; the benchmarked v0.2.26 may predate it (HEAD Project.toml is v0.2.30; which release first carries the fix is not documented). First calls also pay JIT/precompile latency.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Octavian.jl or PureBLAS.jl when your bottleneck is solving small dense systems (LU) rather than GEMM, and over ReLAPACK or BLASFEO when you are already in Julia and want a recursive getrf without linking a C/Fortran LAPACK; from C++ those two are the relevant choices.
verified_claims_summary: On SciML's CI runner (128-thread AMD EPYC 7502, Julia 1.12.7, RecursiveFactorization v0.2.26 via LinearSolve 5.5.0, OpenBLAS_jll 0.3.29, MKL_jll 2025.2.0, BLAS threads set to min(cores, nthreads)), RFLUFactorization reached roughly 33 GFLOPS at N=500 against about 18 for OpenBLAS and 23 for MKL, and about 2x OpenBLAS near N=200-240; values are read off a plot, and MKL beats it at a few noisy sizes.
status_note: Actively maintained by the SciML/JuliaLinearAlgebra maintainers (v0.2.30, last commit 2026-08-09) and MIT-licensed; usable from Julia only, and it depends on LoopVectorization, which is kept alive through SciML small grants.
